5. Name and parentage of accused : 1. Vikas  S/o Late Sh. Gyan Dutt  2. Akash  S/o Late Sh. Gyan Dutt  3. Gyan Dutt  S/o Sh. Durga Prasad  (Proceedings against  him are already abated  vide order dated  08.03.2022)
6. Offense complained or proved : 323/325/341/34 IPC 7.
Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty 8. Date on which order was reserved : 18.03.2024 9.
Final order : Acquitted 10. Date of final order : 16.04.2024 1.
The accused persons namely, Vikas and Akash are facing trial for offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.

The genesis of the prosecution story is that on 22.03.2013 at around 08:40 PM at street in front of H. No. L-690 in front of park, Mangolpuri, Delhi, both the accused persons alongwith their co-accused Gyan Dutt (since dead) in furtherance of common intention of each other stopped the State vs Vikas Etc on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74140350/
1 son of complainant namely, Amit by restraining his way and thereafter, all accused persons started giving beatings to him.
The complainant when intervened in the matter, was also given beatings by the accused persons and the accused Vikas also threw a brick upon him due to which he suffered injury on his arm.

It is also in the allegations that the mother of complainant namely, Surji Devi was also given beatings by the complainant and the complainant and his family members were rescued by the neighbours dwelling in the vicinity.
The accused persons also extended threats of dire consequences to the complainant and his family members.

The complainant alongwith his mother and son were rushed to hospital where they were medically examined and pursuant to the statement given by the complainant, the criminal law was set into motion vide registration of the present FIR.

During the course of investigation, final opinion qua the injuries suffered by the complainant, his son or his mother was obtained, as per which the injuries suffered by the complainant were opined to be grievous in nature and the injuries suffered by his son and mother were opined as simple in nature.

After completion of the investigation, the present charge-sheet was filed for conducting the trial of accused persons for the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.
2.
After taking cognizance of the offences, the copy of charge-sheet was supplied to accused persons in compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C.
The arguments on charges were heard and charges for offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC were framed against accused persons.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed and trial.
Thereafter, prosecution evidence was led.
3. In order to prove allegations against accused persons, prosecution has examined 12 prosecution witnesses.
4. During the pendency of the present case, accused Gyan Dutt unfortunately passed away and the proceedings against him were abated on 08.03.2022.
The case thereafter continued further with respect to other accused persons.
5. After the prosecution evidence, the statements of accused Vikas and Akash u/s 313 Cr.PC were also recorded wherein all the incriminating evidences were put to them.
The accused persons claimed innocence and opted to lead defence evidence.
During the defence evidence, accused persons also examined three defence witnesses to refute the allegations leveled against them.
6. Ld. APP for the State assisted by the Counsel for complainant have argued that prosecution witnesses have supported the prosecution case and their testimonies have remained unrebutted.
It has been further argued that on the combined reading of the testimonies of all the prosecution witnesses, offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC have been proved beyond doubt.

7. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for accused persons has stated that there is no legally sustainable evidence against the accused persons and that the accused persons have been falsely implicated by the police officials at the behest of complainant.

Arguing further, Ld. counsel for accused persons has inter-alia submitted that the present case FIR has been falsely registered against the accused persons at the instance of complainant who was also serving as a police officer during the relevant period.

It has been specifically argued that on the date of alleged incident, the complainant was under the influence of alcohol and stopped accused Vikas and raised demand for money and upon State vs Vikas Etc on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74140350/
2 his refusal, he alongwith his sons falsely implicated the accused persons in the present case.

sentences.text: It is also argued that even the complainant has also made considerable improvements in his version before the Court and the prosecution has also failed to produce any independent eye witnesses to the alleged incident.
It is further argued that due to the lacunae and incoherency in the story of the prosecution, accused persons be given the benefit of doubt and are therefore, entitled to be acquitted.
8. Prior to delving into the contentions raised by the prosecution and defence, let us discuss the testimonies of the material prosecution and defence witnesses in brief.
PW-1/Shankar Lal is the complainant in the present case.

He deposed that on 22.03.2013 at about 8:00 PM, while he was present in his house, he received a call on his mobile phone from his son Jitender that the accused persons were beating him in the park with the help of other goons.
He thereafter tried to make call at 100 number immediately and in the meantime, his other son Amit rushed to the park to save his brother.
He further deposed that his son Jitender manage to flee away from the park with the help of some public persons and came back to the house from the other way.
He further deposed that when his son Amit was on his way, he was captured by the accused persons in the street and they started beating him.
Thereafter, he also came out from the house and found the accused persons present there and witnessed that they were beating his son Amit.
He further deposed that his mother Surji Devi and son Monu @ Mohan were also present there in front of his house and they were also beaten by the accused persons.
He further deposed that thereafter the accused persons also gave beatings to him.

He deposed that accused Gian Dutt caught hold of him from waist, accused Akash caught hold of his right hand and accused Vikas started beating him with a brick and in the meanwhile, public persons intervened and all the accused persons fled away from the spot.
He deposed that thereafter, he, his mother and three sons went to SGM hospital.
He volunteered that he was taken to hospital on motorcycle by someone and his family members were taken in the PCR.
He deposed that he was also threatened by one of the police official who stated that the accused persons made the police call first.
He deposed that the blood was oozing from his left elbow due to injury.
He further deposed that his statement Ex. PW-1/A was recorded by HC Manoj but he could not complete the same and informed the police that he would be making a detailed statement after the treatment.
He stated that there was no particular reason behind the incident.

He deposed that on 27.04.2012, one Bharat Bhushan @ Babbu came to him and informed that the accused persons used to harass him due to which he met the accused Vikas in his shop for making him understand but accused did not pay any heed to his requests after which, he took the above-named Babbu to Police Station on 29.04.2012 and produced him before the SHO where the complaint was filed by him.

He further deposed that thereafter few days, he was called at police station for compromising the matter and he went there on request of father of Babbu and at that time SI Mukesh Antil who was present there threatened him that he was conspirator of the incident but the compromise took place.
He deposed that since then, the accused persons started to threaten him and he made several complaints against them including an application U/s 156 (3) Cr.PC.

He further deposed that even on 26.12.2012, some goons at the instance of the accused persons pelted stones in the street after taking his name and a separate complaint in that regard was filed by him,
due to which the incident dated 23.03.213 had taken place.
During his cross-examination, he could not state about the name of the public persons who saved his son Jitender in the park.

He admitted State vs Vikas Etc on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74140350/
3 of having not made any complaint against HC Manoj specifically.
He stated of having mentioned the manner of the offence in his statement Ex. PW-1/A.
He deposed that the fact that Monu was beaten was not mentioned in his statement as the police did not record his further statement.
He stated that his neighbour Rajesh Kumar took him to hospital.
He admitted that his statement does not find mention of the pre-planned attack and the motive behind the incident.
He stated that the other complaints against the accused persons regarding the threatening were also made by him.
He stated that the police did not ask him to provide the details of the mobile phone number on which his son Jitender called him.
He admitted that he has not mentioned about the reasons of beating his son Jitender by the accused persons.
He admitted that the MLC of his son Jitender was not prepared.
He volunteered that the doctor refused to examine him.
He admitted that no complaint was made by him against the said doctor for such refusal.
He admitted that one FIR U/s 376 IPC was registered against his son Amit.
He admitted of having informed police officers that his son Amit was in street in front of his house.
He stated that the police did not ask about the names of neighbours who were present at the time of incident.
He denied that demand for money was made by him from accused Vikas and upon his refusal, he was threatened to be implicated in a false case.
He denied that the false MLCs were prepared by him by having links with the doctors as he was a police official.

PW-2 Monu is the son of complainant, who deposed that on 22.03.2013, he alongwith his father,
grandmother and brother Amit was present at the house and on that day his another brother Jitender made a phone call to his father and informed that he was beaten by accused persons in the park, after which his brother went to save him and his father also left the house in some time.

He deposed that he alongwith his grandmother remained at the house and after some time, he heard a noise from the street, upon which he and his grandmother went outside and saw that the accused persons beating his father with kicks and blows.
Thereafter, he and his grandmother went to save his father, upon which the accused persons also gave beatings to them and accused Vikas picked up the brick and hit on the left hand of his father.
He deposed that he, his father and grandmother were treated at SGM Hospital.
He identified all the accused persons in Court.
During his cross-examination, he could not state whether he had informed the time of incident to the police.
He admitted of having not seen the quarrel between his brother Jitender and accused persons at the park.

He admitted that at the time of quarrel with his brother Amit, neighbours were also present at the spot and also that at the time of quarrel between his brother Jitender and accused persons neighbours were present at the spot.
He admitted that his father was deputed in PCR van on the relevant date.
He could not state about the period of his admission in the hospital.
He admitted that there are harsh relations between his family and accused persons.
He denied that the accused persons did not give beatings to his brother, father, grandmother or himself.
He denied that the accused persons have been falsely implicated by him at the instance of his father.
PW-3 Jitender is another son of complainant.
He deposed that on 22.03.2013 at about 8:00 PM, all the accused persons came to the park and apprehended him, after which they gave beatings to him.
He stated that his family was having previous enmity with the accused persons.
He deposed of having escaped from the spot and made call to his father upon which his brother Amit came to save him.
He deposed that his brother was also apprehended by the accused persons and beatings were given to him.

He deposed that thereafter, his father was also given beatings by the accused persons and further when his grandmother and other brother Monu came out of the house, they were also State vs Vikas Etc on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74140350/
4 beaten by the accused persons and accused Vikas also hit his father by throwing brick upon him and a PCR call was made, after which the accused persons fled away from the spot.
During his cross-examination
, he admitted of having quareled with his father after escaping from the spot and said fact was also narrated by him to the IO.
He admitted that the neighbours were also present in the park.
He stated that the accused persons entered in the park along with their 20-25 associates.
He admitted that the police had not made any of his neighbour as a witness in the present case.
He could not state about the mobile phone number from which, he made call to his father.
He admitted that his MLC was not prepared.

He also admitted that the neighbours also gathered at the street and name of no such neighbour was narrated by him to the police.
PW-4
Surji Devi is the mother of the complainant.
She deposed that on 22.03.2013 at about 8:00 PM while she was present at her house, her son Shankar Lal told her that the accused persons were beating his grandson Jitender in the park.
She deposed that her grandson Amit went to save Jitender and her son Shankar Lal also ran behind him to save Jitender.

The accused persons apprehended her grandson Amit at the turn of the street near the park and started beating him and at that time when her son Shankar Lal also went outside, the accused persons came in front of her house and started beating her son Shankar Lal.
She deposed that when she alongwith her grandson Monu came out of the house, accused persons also gave them beatings.
She further deposed that accused Vikas hit his son Shankar Lal by throwing the brick.
She deposed that she was saved by the neighbours.
She identified all the accused persons in the Court.
During her cross-examination, she could not state which neighbours were present at the spot.
She denied that she was not present at the spot or that she had not seen the accused persons beating her son and the grandsons.

PW-5 ASI Mahi Lal is a formal witness, who deposed that pursuant to receiving rukka through HC Jitender, he registered FIR Ex. PW-5/B after making endorsement on rukka Ex. PW- 5/A. PW-6 Amit is the son of complainant.

He deposed that on 22.03.2013 he was present at his house alongwith his father Shankar Lal, grandmother Surji Devi and younger brother Monu and at about 8:00 PM, his brother Jitender made a phone call at the mobile phone of his father informing that he was being beaten by accused persons at the park near the house and there upon he ran towards the park and saw that the accused persons were beating his brother Jitender.
He deposed that he shouted and all the three accused persons came towards him and started beating him with fists and kick blows.
He further deposed that in the meantime, his father also shouted from the nearby place and came for releasing him and was also beaten by the accused persons.
He further deposed that his grandmother and younger brother Monu was also beaten by the accused persons when they came to rescue them.
He further deposed that accused Vikas threw a brick upon his father leading to injuries on his left hand and on hearing the noises, the neighbours also gathered at the spot.

He deposed that all the accused persons were arrested in his presence vide arrest memos Ex. PW-5/A to Ex. PW-5/C,
respectively.
During his cross-examination
, he admitted that the public persons were present in the park.
He admitted that the police did not make any inquiry from his neighbours.
He admitted that his father was employed in Delhi Police and was posted in PCR.
He denied that his father misused his official position for preparing the MLCs.
He denied that the incident had never taken place or that he has falsely implicated the accused persons at the instance of his father as the accused Vikas refused to pay money demanded by his father.

Gauri Shankar deposed that on 22.03.2013 while he was present in his house, then at about 8:30 PM, he heard a noise from the street and when he reached outside, quarrel was taking place.

He deposed that accused Gyan Dutt alongwith his sons Vikas and Akash was beatings Shankar Lal,

On the intervention of public persons, the accused persons fled away from the spot and in the said quarrel Shankar Lal,

During his cross-examination, he admitted that he did not see the accused persons beating the complainant and his family members.

PW-8 Ct. Satender is a formal witness, who deposed that the information with respect to the alleged incident was reduced by him in roznamancha vide DD No. 31PP which is Ex. PW-8/A. PW-9 HC Jitender is the police official who arrived at the spot after the alleged incident.
Through his testimony, personal search memos of accused persons were proved on record vide Ex. PW-9/A to Ex. PW-9/C.
PW-10 ASI Manoj Kumar is the IO in the present case.
He deposed about the proceedings conducted by him.
Through his testimony, rukka was exhibited as Ex. PW-10/A and site plan as Ex. PW-10/B.

During his cross-examination, he admitted that complainant informed him that many neighbours gathered at the time of incident and saved him but he did not provide the names of said neighbours except Gauri Shankar.
He admitted that the officials of PCR staff were not made witnesses in the case.
He also admitted that no weapon of offence was recovered in the present case.
PW-11 Dr. Amitabh Bhasin is the medical expert, who proved on record the X-Ray report of complainant Shankar Lal as Ex. PW-11/A. PW-12

respectively.
This is the entire prosecution evidence.
As far as the defence evidence is concerned, the accused persons have examined three defence witnesses in the present case.

DW-1 Pradeep Kumar deposed that he was having cable operator work in Mangolpuri area and on 22.03.2013 at around 8:00 PM he was repairing the broken cables in L-Block and at that time somebody was going on motorcycle and he stopped upon being asked by another person.
The name of motorcyclist was accused Vikas who lived in L-Block and the person who stopped him was complainant Shankar Lal, who was under the influence of alcohol and demanded money from him.

He deposed that upon refusal of accused Vikas to give money to Shankar Lal, he started abusing him and upon his objections, he became furious and after slapping the accused, he threatened him on dire consequences.
Thereafter, his sons Amit and Jitender also came there armed with dandas and started giving beatings to Vikas.
The elder brother and father of accused also arrived there and the complainant and his sons also gave beatings to them.
He deposed that the mother of complainant Surji Devi also gave a brick blow to Vikas after which some body called the police.
During his cross-examination
, he deposed that he could make out from the walk of complainant that he was under the influence of alcohol.

He further deposed that on 22.03.2013 when he was present at his house at 8:00 PM, he heard a noise and came out and saw that Jitender and Amit were carrying dandas and were giving beatings to Vikas.
He deposed that after some time, father and brother of Vikas also came there and they were also beaten by the complainant and his son.
During cross-examination, he stated that around 30-35 persons gathered at the place of incident.

He also deposed that the other neighbours including Sant Ram, Sonu etc.
were also present at the spot.
DW-3 Jai Prakash deposed that on 22.03.2013 at around 7- 7:30 PM while he was walking in the park after dinner, the alleged incident never took place.

He deposed that some public persons gathered outside the park and after hearing some noise he went there and noticed that complainant Shankar alongwith his sons Amit and Jitender were beating Vikas and after some time the brother of Vikas also came there.
During his cross- examination, he could not state the names of all the persons present at the spot except Shashi Bhushan and Pradeep.
He further deposed that around 10-12 persons were also present in the park and there was another park in his locality which is around 200-300 meters away.
He denied of deposing falsely at the instance of accused persons.
This is the entire evidence on record.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE AND CONSEQUENT FINDINGS:
9. I have bestowed my thoughtful consideration to the rival submissions made by both the parties.

Accused persons have been indicted for the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.
10.

For the sake of repetition, it is again reiterated that the sum and substance of the allegations as levelled against accused persons is that on 22.03.2013 at about 8:40 PM in the Street of H. No. L-690, in front of Park, Mangolpuri, Delhi, all accused persons in furtherance of common intention of each other wrongfully restrained the son of complainant Jitender and caused simple injuries on his person.

The allegations are also to the extent that all the accused persons also gave beatings to the complainant Shankar Lal and his other son Monu and mother Surji Devi when they tried to rescue the victim Jitender and caused grievous injuries to complainant Shankar Lal and simple injuries to Monu and Surji Devi and thereby committed offences punishable u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.
11.

The careful perusal of the case record would reflect that in order to establish the guilt of the accused, the prosecution is primarily relying upon the testimonies of PW-1 Shankar Lal, PW-2 Monu, PW-3 Jitender, PW-4 Surji Devi, PW-6 Amit and PW-7 Gauri Shanker.

It is pertinent to mention that PWs 2, 3 & 6 are the sons of the complainant and PW-4 is the mother of complainant whereas, PW-7 Gauri Shankar is one of the neighbour who is stated to be dwelling in the same vicinity where the alleged incident had taken place.

The careful perusal of the testimonies of PWs 1, 2, 3,
State vs Vikas Etc on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74140350/
7 4 & 6 suggests that the relationship between the complainant, his family members and the accused persons was not cordial.

The complainant has himself admitted that fact that even prior to the alleged incident, he filed a complaint and an application U/s 156 (3) Cr.PC against the accused persons as the accused persons and the goons sent by them pelted stones in the street after taking his name, as he helped one Bharat Bhushan @ Babbu, who was harassed by the accused persons.

In similar manner, PW-2 Monu, PW-3 Jitender, PW-6 Amit (all sons of complainant) and PW-4 Surji Devi have also admitted the fact that the relationship between the family of the complainant and the accused persons was not cordial.

It is further pertinent to mention that during their deposition, PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4 and PW-6 have categorically admitted the fact that at the time of incident at the park when the accused persons were beating the son of complainant Jitender (PW-3) and thereafter,
i.e. when the complainant alongwith his mother and other son Monu tried to rescue Jitender, the public persons were present.
Even during the testimony of PW-9 HC Jitender and IO ASI Manoj Kumar examined as PW-10, it has come that when the police arrived at the spot, several public persons were present there.
Surprisingly, no such public persons except one i.e. PW-7 Gauri Shankar have been cited as witnesses in the present case.

PW-10 has though tried to give justification that he did not examine any other public persons or neighbours from the vicinity qua the alleged incident as complainant only disclosed about the name of PW Gauri Shankar to him but the said justification given by the IO does not inspire confidence as it was incumbent on his part to associate the public persons as the witnesses in the present case when he himself acquired the knowledge that several public persons were present at the time of the alleged incident.

The fact that the relationship between the complainant, his family and the accused persons was not cordial and the animosity between the parties was upto such an extent that the complainant already filed various complaints against them, hence, in view of such strained relations between the parties, it would not be safe to rely upon the testimony of the complainant and his family members solely without any corroboration with the other independent evidences, as the complainant and his family members naturally appear to be interested witnesses.
The prosecution has only examined one so called independent witness for establishing the allegations levelled against the accused persons.
PW-7 Gauri Shankar who is stated to be the neighbour dwelling the in same vicinity has been examined by the prosecution to prove its story.
The mere perusal of the testimony of PW-7 suggests that when he arrived at spot after hearing the loud noise, a quarrel was going on between the complainant, his sons and the accused persons.

Pertinently, this witness did not state as to who had initiated the alleged quarrel between the parties and what was the cause of the same and rather deposed only to the extent that when he reached the spot, the quarrel was already going on.

Therefore, the testimony of this witness also appears to be hearsay in nature and does not establish the story of prosecution that the alleged quarrel was initiated by the accused persons when they attacked the son of complainant at the park and thereafter, assaulted the complainant and his family members, when they tried to rescue the son of complainant.

The accused persons have propounded the defence that they have been falsely implicated by the complainant on account of refusal of accused Vikas to provide him money for purchasing liquor and the said defence appears to be satisfactorily established by the accused persons through the testimonies of DWs 1 and 2.

sentences.text: specifically, DW-1 Pradeep Kumar and DW-2 Shashi Bhushan
have coherently deposed that the complainant Shankar Lal raised unlawful demands for money from accused Vikas due to which he has falsely implicated the accused persons in the present case.
Nothing discrediting the version of defence witnesses could be brought before the Court despite their extensive and detailed cross-examination conducted by the prosecution.

It is also pertinent to mention that during the testimony of PW-12 Dr. Beena, it has astonishingly come before the Court that apart from the MLC of complainant Shankar Lal, she also issued MLCs of two other persons namely Meenu and Sojji who were brought for examination with respect to the alleged incident but the prosecution has failed to disclose as to in what manner the above named Meenu and Sojji were related to the complainant and there is no mention qua any assault/injuries inflicted upon them by the accused persons in the entire chargesheet, which also probablizes the defence of accused persons that the complainant being a police official might have exerted his official influence and got managed the false MLCs from the concerned hospital, so as to falsely implicate the accused persons in the present case.

The evidences on record are not sufficient to bring home the guilt of accused persons for the alleged offences and rather from the inconsistencies in the version of the material prosecution witnesses, it reflects that the story propounded by the complainant is false and there leaves no room for doubt that the prosecution case is nothing but a false and concocted set of facts based on the bundle of lies made by the complainant.

This Court is well cognizant of the fact that the minor contradictions in the testimonies of witnesses which does not go to the root of the case deserves to be ignored but conversely, the material contradictions and omissions in the testimony of witnesses which goes to and attacks the very roots of the case cannot be ignored.

It is also a settled canon of criminal jurisprudence that if two reasonably probable and evenly balanced views of the evidence are possible, one must necessarily concede to the existence of a reasonable doubt.

The aforementioned lacunae in the story of the prosecution render the version of the prosecution doubtful, leading to the irresistible conclusion that the burden of proving the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubts has not been discharged by the prosecution.

Thus, this Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to bring on record any cogent evidence in order to prove the commission and guilt of the accused persons for offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC beyond reasonable doubts, thus, entitling the accused persons to benefit of doubt and acquittal.
12. Accordingly, this Court hereby accords the benefit of doubt to the accused persons for the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC and holds the accused persons not guilty for the alleged offences.

The accused persons namel,y Vikas and Akash, are thus, acquitted of the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.

It is also in the allegations that the mother of complainant namely, Surji Devi was also given beatings by the complainant and the complainant and his family members were rescued by the neighbours dwelling in the vicinity.
The accused persons also extended threats of dire consequences to the complainant and his family members.
The complainant alongwith his mother and son were rushed to hospital where they were medically examined and pursuant to the statement given by the complainant, the criminal law was set into motion vide registration of the present FIR.
During the course of investigation, final opinion qua the injuries suffered by the complainant, his son or his mother was obtained, as per which the injuries suffered by the complainant were opined to be grievous in nature and the injuries suffered by his son and mother were opined as simple in nature.
After completion of the investigation, the present charge-sheet was filed for conducting the trial of accused persons for the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.
2.
After taking cognizance of the offences, the copy of charge-sheet was supplied to accused persons in compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C.
The arguments on charges were heard and charges for offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC were framed against accused persons.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed and trial.
5. After the prosecution evidence, the statements of accused Vikas and Akash u/s 313 Cr.PC were also recorded wherein all the incriminating evidences were put to them.
The accused persons claimed innocence and opted to lead defence evidence.
During the defence evidence, accused persons also examined three defence witnesses to refute the allegations leveled against them.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
6. Ld. APP for the State assisted by the Counsel for complainant have argued that prosecution witnesses have supported the prosecution case and their testimonies have remained unrebutted.
It has been further argued that on the combined reading of the testimonies of all the prosecution witnesses, offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC have been proved beyond doubt.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The allegations are also to the extent that all the accused persons also gave beatings to the complainant Shankar Lal and his other son Monu and mother Surji Devi when they tried to rescue the victim Jitender and caused grievous injuries to complainant Shankar Lal and simple injuries to Monu and Surji Devi and thereby committed offences punishable u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.
11.
The careful perusal of the testimonies of PWs 1, 2, 3,
State vs Vikas Etc on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74140350/
7 4 & 6 suggests that the relationship between the complainant, his family members and the accused persons was not cordial.
The complainant has himself admitted that fact that even prior to the alleged incident, he filed a complaint and an application U/s 156 (3) Cr.PC against the accused persons as the accused persons and the goons sent by them pelted stones in the street after taking his name, as he helped one Bharat Bhushan @ Babbu, who was harassed by the accused persons.
PW-10 has though tried to give justification that he did not examine any other public persons or neighbours from the vicinity qua the alleged incident as complainant only disclosed about the name of PW Gauri Shankar to him but the said justification given by the IO does not inspire confidence as it was incumbent on his part to associate the public persons as the witnesses in the present case when he himself acquired the knowledge that several public persons were present at the time of the alleged incident.
The fact that the relationship between the complainant, his family and the accused persons was not cordial and the animosity between the parties was upto such an extent that the complainant already filed various complaints against them, hence, in view of such strained relations between the parties, it would not be safe to rely upon the testimony of the complainant and his family members solely without any corroboration with the other independent evidences, as the complainant and his family members naturally appear to be interested witnesses.
The prosecution has only examined one so called independent witness for establishing the allegations levelled against the accused persons.
The mere perusal of the testimony of PW-7 suggests that when he arrived at spot after hearing the loud noise, a quarrel was going on between the complainant, his sons and the accused persons.
Therefore, the testimony of this witness also appears to be hearsay in nature and does not establish the story of prosecution that the alleged quarrel was initiated by the accused persons when they attacked the son of complainant at the park and thereafter, assaulted the complainant and his family members, when they tried to rescue the son of complainant.
The accused persons have propounded the defence that they have been falsely implicated by the complainant on account of refusal of accused Vikas to provide him money for purchasing liquor and the said defence appears to be satisfactorily established by the accused persons through the testimonies of DWs 1 and 2.
have coherently deposed that the complainant Shankar Lal raised unlawful demands for money from accused Vikas due to which he has falsely implicated the accused persons in the present case.
Nothing discrediting the version of defence witnesses could be brought before the Court despite their extensive and detailed cross-examination conducted by the prosecution.
It is also pertinent to mention that during the testimony of PW-12 Dr. Beena, it has astonishingly come before the Court that apart from the MLC of complainant Shankar Lal, she also issued MLCs of two other persons namely Meenu and Sojji who were brought for examination with respect to the alleged incident but the prosecution has failed to disclose as to in what manner the above named Meenu and Sojji were related to the complainant and there is no mention qua any assault/injuries inflicted upon them by the accused persons in the entire chargesheet, which also probablizes the defence of accused persons that the complainant being a police official might have exerted his official influence and got managed the false MLCs from the concerned hospital, so as to falsely implicate the accused persons in the present case.
The evidences on record are not sufficient to bring home the guilt of accused persons for the alleged offences and rather from the inconsistencies in the version of the material prosecution witnesses, it reflects that the story propounded by the complainant is false and there leaves no room for doubt that the prosecution case is nothing but a false and concocted set of facts based on the bundle of lies made by the complainant.
This Court is well cognizant of the fact that the minor contradictions in the testimonies of witnesses which does not go to the root of the case deserves to be ignored but conversely, the material contradictions and omissions in the testimony of witnesses which goes to and attacks the very roots of the case cannot be ignored.
It is also a settled canon of criminal jurisprudence that if two reasonably probable and evenly balanced views of the evidence are possible, one must necessarily concede to the existence of a reasonable doubt.
The aforementioned lacunae in the story of the prosecution render the version of the prosecution doubtful, leading to the irresistible conclusion that the burden of proving the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubts has not been discharged by the prosecution.
Thus, this Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to bring on record any cogent evidence in order to prove the commission and guilt of the accused persons for offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC beyond reasonable doubts, thus, entitling the accused persons to benefit of doubt and acquittal.
opennyai_summary.decision:
12. Accordingly, this Court hereby accords the benefit of doubt to the accused persons for the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC and holds the accused persons not guilty for the alleged offences.
The accused persons namel,y Vikas and Akash, are thus, acquitted of the offences u/s 323/325/341/34 IPC.
